newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard calls on Senator Colston to stand aside.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard calls on Senator Colston to stand aside.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Tuesday urged Senator Mal Colston, an independent crucial to the legislative programme, to stand aside as deputy Senate president while allegations of dishonest expense claims are investigated.

"Senator Colston should stand down as deputy president of the Senate and all of the matters in dispute relating to his travelling allowance should be referred to the Federal Police," Howard told reporters.
The year-old Liberal-National government, pushing a programme of economic reform, is two votes short of a majority in the Senate, the upper house of parliament.

Colston, who has denied any wrongdoing, defected from the Labor opposition in August and has since joined another independent to supply those two votes, letting the government slash the budget deficit and sell a third of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp.
But a former staff member accused the key senator in February of misusing expense allowances and of giving office jobs to relatives who did no work.
Senate officials have also found that he had wrongly claimed a travelling allowance.
Another staff member took responsibility for the error, saying she had kept poor records and prepared incorrect claims. But that staff member, Christine Smith, recanted on Tuesday.

Opposition Senate Leader John Faulkner on Tuesday produced a letter in which Smith said: "I was not responsible for preparing the senator's travelling allowance claims nor required to keep a record of dates of travel for (travelling allowance) purposes.
"The senator always prepared his own claims," Smith said.
